title: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis After Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplantation
off: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Multicenter Ambispective Longitudinal Cohort Study

officials.a: Peking University Institute of Hematology, Peking University People's Hospital

summary:
Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a severe inflammatory complication that can occur after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Its signs can overlap with those of infection and other transplant complications, making early recognition difficult. This study will examine whether changes in routine blood tests and clinical information can help identify patients who may develop HLH during the following seven days.

The study will combine a review of existing medical records with prospective follow-up at participating hospitals in China. Approximately 20,000 adults undergoing their first allogeneic transplantation will be included, with approximately 400 post-transplant HLH cases expected. Historical records will be used to develop the prediction model. Data from independent centers and prospectively enrolled patients will be used to validate the model.

Participants will be followed for one year after transplantation. Those who develop HLH during that year will also be followed for 90 days after HLH onset. The study will describe HLH occurrence, associated factors, treatments, and survival. All tests and treatments will remain part of routine care. No additional research samples or laboratory tests will be required, and model predictions will not be used to guide treatment.
desc:
This multicenter ambispective longitudinal observational cohort study will characterize de novo hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) and develop and independently validate a dynamic model for HLH occurrence within the next seven days. Eligible participants are adults aged 18 years or older at their first allo-HSCT. Patients with HLH diagnosed before transplantation or transplantation performed primarily for HLH are excluded.

The retrospective component includes first allo-HSCT performed from January 1, 2014, through the day before prospective study activation at each center. Records available before activation will be reviewed. A stratified case-cohort design will be used: a 15% random subcohort will be selected within center and transplant-year strata, and all eligible HLH cases in the source cohort will be included in the detailed analysis. Patients belonging to both the random subcohort and the HLH case set will be counted once. Basic transplant and outcome information will be collected for the source cohort.

The prospective component will consecutively enroll eligible patients after ethics approval and site activation through December 31, 2029. Written informed consent will be obtained before transplantation, and participants will enter the transplant cohort after the procedure is completed. Additional research follow-up of retrospectively identified patients will require written informed consent. The planned combined source cohort comprises approximately 20,000 recipients, including approximately 400 expected HLH cases.

Data collection includes underlying disease and disease status, comorbidities, donor and transplant characteristics, conditioning, graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis, engraftment, infections, viral reactivation, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease, organ dysfunction, and treatments. Longitudinal routine laboratory data include blood counts, ferritin, C-reactive protein, fibrinogen, triglycerides, D-dimer, lactate dehydrogenase, albumin, and liver and kidney function. Cytokines, soluble CD25, and natural killer cell function results will be recorded when obtained during routine care. Sampling times, result availability times, units, and reference ranges will be retained.

The primary clinical outcome is the first de novo HLH episode within 365 days after allo-HSCT. An episode must meet at least five of the eight HLH-2004 criteria during the same clinical episode and be confirmed by the adjudication group. Two investigators will independently review potential cases, with a third investigator resolving disagreement. The onset date is the earliest date on which the study definition is fulfilled. Dates of first clinical suspicion, clinical diagnosis, and HLH-directed treatment initiation will also be recorded. Clinically diagnosed episodes not meeting the primary definition will be recorded separately for supplementary analyses. Adjudicators will not have access to new-model predictions. Death and second allogeneic transplantation before HLH will be treated as competing events.

At evaluable assessment times from day 1 through day 358 after transplantation, information already available at that time will be used to predict first HLH onset within the subsequent seven days. Model evaluation will use assessments obtained before HLH onset and before initiation of HLH-directed treatment. Models and thresholds will be fixed before independent-center and prospective validation. Prospective predictions will be recorded for research and will not be provided to treating teams as treatment decision prompts.

Follow-up will continue through one year after transplantation. Clinical and outcome information will be reviewed monthly during the first six months and at months 9 and 12; routine inpatient data will be collected longitudinally. For participants who develop HLH during the first year, additional assessments will be recorded on days 7, 14, 28, 60, and 90 after HLH onset. Follow-up will use hospital and outpatient records, telephone, online or video contact, or in-person visits. Patients developing HLH late in the first year may be followed for up to approximately 15 months after transplantation.

Analyses will account for case-cohort sampling, competing events, center, and transplant period. Dynamic landmark models, penalized regression, and gradient boosting will be evaluated. Inflammatory characteristics will be examined using representative subcohort data and compared with clinical and simplified models. Performance will be assessed using discrimination, calibration, Brier scores, decision curves, case detection, positive predictive value, warning lead time, and false-alert frequency. Secondary analyses will describe HLH triggers, organ support, treatment patterns, recorded early treatment response, and survival.

The study does not assign treatment or require additional blood sampling, laboratory tests, or biospecimen retention. Historical records will be used under the applicable ethics-approved consent or waiver procedures; prospective participants will provide written informed consent. Each site will retain its identity linkage file. The coordinating database will receive coded data without direct personal identifiers, and results will be reported in aggregate.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older at first allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

First allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation performed at a participating center within the study period.

Verifiable transplantation date and basic clinical information. Written informed consent from the participant or legally authorized representative for prospective participation. Retrospective records are used under the applicable ethics-approved consent or waiver procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Autologous transplantation or transplantation other than hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

HLH diagnosed before transplantation, or transplantation performed primarily for HLH.

Previous allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient identity, transplantation date, or key outcome information cannot be verified.

Explicit refusal to participate or to permit the use of clinical information for this study.

x.titre: Risque de LHH à 7 jours après allogreffe : cohorte multicentrique et modèle prédictif
x.question: Peut-on prédire, à partir des examens biologiques courants, la survenue d'une LHH dans les 7 jours suivant une allogreffe de cellules souches ?
x.contexte:
La lymphohistiocytose hémophagocytaire (LHH) est une complication inflammatoire grave pouvant survenir après allogreffe de cellules souches hématopoïétiques. Ses signes (fièvre, cytopénies, hyperferritinémie, atteinte hépatique) recoupent ceux des infections et d'autres complications de la greffe, ce qui retarde le diagnostic.

La fréquence réelle de la LHH post-greffe et ses facteurs de risque restent mal décrits, et aucun outil dynamique ne permet de l'anticiper. Cette étude observationnelle ambispective et multicentrique, promue par l'hôpital universitaire de Pékin, combine l'analyse de dossiers existants (greffes depuis 2014) et un suivi prospectif dans des centres chinois. Elle utilise un schéma cas-cohorte stratifié, avec un sous-échantillon aléatoire de 15 % et tous les cas de LHH. Environ 20 000 adultes à leur première allogreffe sont attendus, dont environ 400 LHH. L'objectif est de décrire l'incidence cumulée et de développer, puis de valider indépendamment, un modèle prédisant la LHH dans les 7 jours suivants à partir des variations biologiques et cliniques.
x.interet: Un modèle validé pourrait aider à repérer plus tôt les receveurs d'allogreffe à risque de LHH et à déclencher un bilan ou un traitement précoce. Il reste à démontrer qu'une alerte précoce améliore le pronostic.
